subject: Split-plane scaling, capacity zones & cutover checklist
snippet: Acme asks for split-plane scaling guidance and a staged cutover checklist for their private VPC; internal thread to align control/data plane placement, capacity zones, and schedule.
messages:
From: Lena Park <lena.park@acme.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya@edgeware.io>
Date: 2026-11-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: split-plane scaling + staged cutover for Acme private VPC

Hi Hannah / Irene,

Thanks again for taking the time on Friday. As we start to lock in the private VPC topology for our on-prem clusters, a couple of asks from our infra team: 

- A concise reference diagram that shows recommended control-plane placement vs. data-plane nodes for a split-plane Redwood deployment (we run 3 racks per site, two sites per region).
- Guidance on capacity zoning (how many data-plane GPUs per zone, expected headroom for burst workloads).
- A staged cutover checklist we can share with our NOC / network teams (preflight checks, firewall rules, BGP peering sanity, certificate rotation steps).

We're aiming for a late-Nov/early-Dec maintenance window but need your checklist to finalize the change freeze and runbook. I've attached our constraints doc that lists rack IP pools, proxy constraints, and a brief list of third-party services that must remain reachable during cutover.

Attachments: acme-deploy-constraints.pdf (pdf)

Appreciate any reference materials or a short template we can use.

-Lena
Lena Park
Head of Platform Engineering | Acme Corp

Lena — thanks for the constraints doc, that helps a lot. High level we can deliver:

1) A 1-page reference diagram (control-plane placement, control-plane proxies, data-plane zones, egress points).
2) A capacity zoning recommendation based on your 3-rack per site topology: baseline + 30% burst headroom guidance.
3) A staged cutover checklist (preflight, staged traffic migration, rollback gates, observability smoke tests).

Internal owners:

- Verification tests (latency/cost samples): Marcus (simulation and traffic shaping tests)

Proposed timeline: we can give you a first-pass reference doc and checklist by EOD Wednesday (2026-11-24). Are you targeting a specific UTC window for the maintenance? If so call it out and we'll align the rollback gates accordingly.

I'll attach my notes from the initial read of the constraints for internal context.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head, Infra Partnerships | Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena Park <lena@acme.com>
Date: 2026-11-23T14:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: split-plane scaling + staged cutover for Acme private VPC

Folks — attaching a first-pass reference diagram (reference-diagram-v1.svg) and inline notes. Quoting Lena at top.

Notes / design decisions (summary):
- Control plane: place a 3-node control-plane cluster per site in the management VLAN; control-plane communicates over private peering to data-plane racks. Keep control-plane public egress minimal (metrics + update checks only).
- Proxies: front control-plane with a pair of HA proxies in each site to avoid single-hop failure during rack-level maintenance.
- Data plane capacity zones: map each rack to a "zone" with at least 1 hot spare GPU rack per zone to absorb node failures during cutover. Recommendation: for your reported workload, target 24 GPU-equivalents per zone baseline, 32 GPU-equivalents for peak-shift headroom.
- KV cache strategy: enable per-zone prefix caching; control-plane should be able to route cache misses to neighboring zone with higher tail latency but still within SLA.
- Network: pre-create BGP sessions and verify route filters; ensure egress NAT for model downloads happens from a controlled IP set (we'll provide the list).

Cutover pitfalls to call out:
- Certificate TTLs: ensure a sub-hour TTL for short-lived certs during cutover to avoid stale sessions.
- Firewall state: planned TCP drain may leave ephemeral state that needs cleanup; add a tcp_repair step to checklist.
- Observability: verify KV cache hitrate and per-token latency before shifting traffic.

I've included inline suggestions on the diagram for where to place egress collectors and tracing hooks. Next: Kimberly will stitch the checklist into a staged XLS with explicit acceptance gates.

Irene Choi
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
Attachments: reference-diagram-v1.svg (image)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@acme.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Split-plane scaling, capacity zones & cutover checklist

Lena — attaching the cutover checklist and a short runbook (cutover-checklist-v1.xlsx). Highlights and plan: 

Planned maintenance window (proposed): 2026-12-05 01:00-05:00 UTC
Preflight (T-72 to T-2 hrs):
- Confirm control-plane nodes healthy and pod restarts < 2% in last 24h
- Validate BGP session establishment to each data-plane edge (test route announce/withdraw)
- Confirm access to model artifact CDN via controlled egress IPs
- Provision & test HA proxies for control-plane (failover test)

Cutover phases:
Phase A — Data-plane warm sync: shard small % traffic to new zone, monitor KV cache hitrate (target >= 85%) and tail p50/p99 latency
Phase B — Bulk traffic shift by zone with 15-minute observation gates
Phase C — Post-shift verification: run 10 synthetic generation tests, compare token latency and token cost delta within thresholds

Rollbacks:
- Immediate: revert traffic steering to previous zone + clear ephemeral firewall states
- Fallback: stand up pre-warmed spare zone (we recommend one spare per site)

Acceptance gates (in XLS): health probes, latency delta thresholds, cost delta threshold, manual sign-off by Acme NOC and Redwood Ops.

Operational notes:
- JIRA ticket ENGOPS-2145 created for the cutover tasks — link in the Drive folder.
- Please confirm the final maintenance window; once confirmed we will circulate the runbook and request DocuSign for operational change approval if your process requires it.

Thanks — Kim
Kimberly Park
Principal Customer Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachments: cutover-checklist-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)
